title: The Orchard of the Old Mill House
premise: Ulyana Ashgrove has built a career on other people's voices, ghostwriting the memoirs of her rival, publishing darling Marguerite Voss, while keeping her own heart locked in the past tense after a devastating early betrayal. When her family's centennial reunion at the crumbling Old Mill House orchard demands she arrive with a partner, she hires quiet arborist Theo Lindqvist through a discreet arrangement to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. But the fake courtship curdles into something real over long dinners and cider-press afternoons, and Ulyana must choose between exposing her ghostwriting secret to claim her own voice and her own love, or staying invisible forever. When Marguerite threatens to reveal Ulyana's authorship and destroy her livelihood, Ulyana publishes the truth herself, and in the orchard's last harvest, she and Theo plant something that will outlast them both.
about_author: Jonah Crane is the pen name of a former orchard worker turned novelist who spent a decade writing other people's stories before claiming one of their own. They live near an abandoned mill house in the Hudson Valley, where the apple trees still bear fruit no one planted.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She finishes drafting Marguerite Voss's memoir at 3 a.m., erasing herself from a life story that is secretly hers to tell. Her editor praises Marguerite's 'voice'—Ulyana's voice. Emotional beat: the ache of invisibility, and the letter from her grandmother summoning the family to the Old Mill House reunion.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Cornered by her mother's ultimatum—bring someone or explain why not—Ulyana finds Theo Lindqvist, a stoic arborist restoring the orchard, and proposes a paid arrangement: one weekend, one fake romance, no questions. Emotional beat: transactional control masking fear of intimacy.

chapters.title: The Interview
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He agrees to the arrangement for money to save his failing nursery, studying Ulyana like a tree with rot hidden under sound bark. Their rehearsal dinner-date feels awkwardly, dangerously easy. Emotional beat: curiosity kindling beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: Gates of the Old Mill House
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They arrive at the decaying family estate where her grandmother rules and old wounds wait in every room. The family immediately interrogates the 'couple.' Theo improvises a story about how they met that is too specific, too true. Emotional beat: the fake begins to bleed into the real.

chapters.title: Cider and Small Wars
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the welcome dinner, her brother's wife needles Ulyana about her 'unambitious' career, and Theo defends her with quiet ferocity she never asked for. Her grandmother watches them both with knowing eyes. Emotional beat: being defended feels like being seen.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo walks the orchard with Ulyana's grandmother, who reveals Ulyana once dreamed of writing under her own name—and that the family's old mill failed because its owners hid the truth to survive. Emotional beat: Theo begins to understand the woman he's pretending to love.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The reunion's final night: a toast, a dance under strung lights, and Theo's hand at her waist feeling less like performance than promise. They almost kiss; she pulls away and names it 'part of the job.' Emotional beat: terror of wanting something real.

chapters.title: The Contract Ends
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Back in the city, the weekend is over but neither can let go. Theo keeps fixing her fire escape; she keeps finding reasons to visit his nursery. Emotional beat: the fiction outliving its deadline.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Draft
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Marguerite demands revisions and drops a threat wrapped in silk: she knows Ulyana has been 'moonlighting,' and a rival publisher is sniffing around authorship of the memoir. Emotional beat: the cage tightening; power corrupting the person who holds it.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ulyana offers Theo a 'real arrangement'—dating without promises, love in installments. He refuses the terms; he has watched trees die from half-measures. Emotional beat: honest refusal, first true rupture between them.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Alone, she rereads her old rejected novel and the letter from the man who once told her love was a liability. She realizes she ghostwrote her own heart out of her life long before Marguerite. Emotional beat: grief reframed as self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's nursery faces foreclosure; his own history of losing everything by betting on people surfaces. He almost signs a deal that would gut the orchard's heirloom trees—a mirror of Ulyana's compromises. Emotional beat: recognizing corruption in oneself.

chapters.title: The Second Invitation
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Grandmother summons Ulyana back to the mill house alone, shows her the orchard's dying central tree, and asks what she intends to save—her name, her work, or herself. Emotional beat: a matriarch's blessing disguised as a challenge.

chapters.title: Blackmail in Bloom
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Marguerite delivers an ultimatum: sign away all credit for the memoir and ghostwrite the sequel, or be exposed as a fraud and sued. She gives Ulyana one week. Emotional beat: cornered, humiliated, furious.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Ulyana finds Theo at the orchard and tells him everything—the ghostwriting, the fake date, the blackmail—and asks him to disappear with her rather than watch her fight. He asks instead why she keeps choosing survival over living. Emotional beat: the whole heart offered, the whole truth demanded.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Mill House
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A storm devastates the orchard the night before her deadline; the family rallies to save the trees, and Ulyana works beside Theo in the rain, hands and guards down. Emotional beat: love against duty, made literal in mud and lightning.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She sits before Marguerite's contract with a pen in hand. Instead of signing, she emails the complete manuscript—under her own name—to the rival publisher who once rejected her, with proof of authorship. Emotional beat: the point of no return, terrifying and clean.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Marguerite's lawyers descend; the industry erupts; Ulyana loses clients, income, and standing overnight. Her family learns the truth of her 'small' career. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, and the strange lightness of ruin.

chapters.title: What Survives a Fire
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo publicly backs Ulyana, sacrificing the nursery deal to protect the heirloom orchard instead, and tells her the words she once couldn't hear: that love isn't a liability. Emotional beat: devotion proven by cost, not declaration.

chapters.title: Byline
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The rival publisher offers her a two-book deal under her own name; the memoir's true authorship becomes the story everyone wants. Her grandmother, dying but lucid, reads Ulyana's acknowledgment page and weeps. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by mortality—time was always running out.

chapters.title: The Last Harvest
chapters.summary: Both POVs. At the mill house, the family gathers for what may be the orchard's final full harvest; Ulyana and Theo press cider together, and she asks him to stay—not as an arrangement, but as a choice. He says yes. Emotional beat: love in present tense at last.

chapters.title: The Orchard of the Old Mill House
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ulyana's POV. One year later: her debut novel under her own name sits in the mill house window; she and Theo plant a new heirloom tree where the old central tree fell. Emotional beat: the price of survival was everything, and it was worth it—roots planted, voice claimed, whole heart given.
